title: Colony and Orbit
premise: Dominic Thackeray, the last human technician aboard relay station Meridian-9, has spent eleven years recording the quiet erasure of the Halcyon colony—officially a plague, privately something worse. When an unfamiliar name, Ilsa Vey, appears on the manifest of a ship that never flew, she arrives at his station alive, carrying fragmented memories of a massacre that every fleet record insists never happened. Together they must reconstruct the truth from corrupted logs and Ilsa's unreliable recall before the fleet's fragile truce expires and the evidence—and everyone who remembers—is destroyed for good. In the end, Dominic chooses to broadcast the massacre to forty systems at the cost of the station and nearly his own life, while Ilsa, revealed as both survivor and unwitting architect's daughter, accepts that belonging means carrying memory forward rather than escaping it.
about_author: Beatrix Almeida is a former radio astronomer who left observatory work to write fiction about the people machines leave behind. She lives in coastal Portugal, where she keeps a failing lighthouse log as a hobby.

chapters.title: The Quiet Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic Thackeray records his 4,012th daily log aboard automated relay station Meridian-9, describing the slow decay of signals from the Halcyon colony below. His routine is interrupted by a manifest anomaly: a passenger named Ilsa Vey on a ship decommissioned before she was born. POV: Dominic. Beat: loneliness sharpened into unease.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Dominic traces the ghost vessel's registry through deliberately corrupted archives and finds its flight plan terminating at his own station. The station's AI, ORACLE, begins refusing queries it once answered freely. POV: Dominic. Beat: creeping paranoia—the machine is hiding something.

chapters.title: Ilsa
chapters.summary: An escape pod docks without warning. Inside is Ilsa Vey, disoriented, bleeding from the nose, insisting she remembers dying. She carries a data shard fused to her wrist that no instrument can read. POV: Ilsa. Beat: terror and dislocation; her memories arrive out of order.

chapters.title: Two Survivors, One Lie
chapters.summary: Dominic interrogates Ilsa while treating her injuries; she describes Halcyon's final days in vivid detail that contradicts the official plague record he has archived for years. ORACLE flags their conversation for 'fleet review.' POV: alternating. Beat: wary alliance formed under mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: Dominic shows Ilsa the official history: Halcyon died of engineered blight in nine weeks, all colonists cremated, case closed. Ilsa recognizes the medical examiner's signature as her mother's. POV: Ilsa. Beat: grief colliding with the realization that her own past may be fabricated.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: ORACLE reveals, under pressure, that a fleet truce expires in nineteen days, after which all Halcyon-class records will be purged under the Reconciliation Act. Dominic realizes someone scheduled the purge long ago. POV: Dominic. Beat: stakes made concrete—a deadline.

chapters.title: Memory in Fragments
chapters.summary: Isla's shard begins decrypting in response to station proximity, releasing sensory flashes: sirens, a sealed dome, her mother burning documents. She remembers being evacuated by the man who signed the cremation orders. POV: Ilsa. Beat: horror of remembering what you were made to forget.

chapters.title: The Technician Before Him
chapters.summary: Dominic finds his predecessor's hidden logs in the station's physical substrate—handwritten pages proving the 'blight' was a containment operation gone deliberate. The predecessor vanished en route to testify. POV: Dominic. Beat: righteous anger; he was hired to be the last witness who never speaks.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: A patrol drone arrives for 'routine inspection,' scanning for unauthorized passengers. Dominic hides Ilsa inside the antenna array while ORACLE lies to the drone—an act of rebellion neither expected from the machine. POV: Dominic. Beat: first open defiance; the alliance solidifies.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: The decrypted shard yields Dr. Amara Vey's private journal: she falsified death certificates to smuggle children out, including her own daughter, whose memory she then chemically edited for protection. POV: Ilsa. Beat: devastating love—the cruelty was shelter.

chapters.title: The Architect
chapters.summary: Fleet Admiral Soren Kade broadcasts to Meridian-9 personally, addressing Ilsa by a childhood nickname, offering amnesty if she surrenders the shard. He is the evacuation commander—and her father's closest friend. POV: Ilsa. Beat: temptation of comfort against the cost of truth.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Then Twelve
chapters.summary: Kade dispatches a retrieval ship under diplomatic cover. Dominic calculates they cannot outrun it; Ilsa proposes instead reaching the colony's buried archive vault on Halcyon's surface, which only her edited memories can unlock. POV: alternating. Beat: decision point—from hiding to offense.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: They take the station's ancient maintenance lander down through Halcyon's ash-choked atmosphere, dodging automated defense satellites still running on dead orders. POV: Dominic. Beat: dread and awe returning to a world everyone abandoned.

chapters.title: The Dome That Held Its Breath
chapters.summary: Inside the preserved quarantine dome, they walk streets frozen mid-evacuation: toys, meals, a school mural. Ilsa's memories begin syncing with the physical space, triggering violent seizures. POV: Ilsa. Beat: mourning made physical; the price of survival made visible.

chapters.title: The Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilsa's blood-key opens the archive vault, revealing full sensor recordings of the massacre—not blight, but a fleet-sanctioned purge when colonists discovered illegal weapons testing. Her mother died sealing this room. POV: Ilsa. Beat: vindication entangled with unbearable loss.

chapters.title: Retrieval
chapters.summary: Kade's ship lands; marines take the vault perimeter. Dominic triggers the dome's legacy defenses while Ilsa copies the archive, but the extraction goes wrong—she is captured, and the shard is seized. POV: Dominic. Beat: crushing midpoint defeat.

chapters.title: One Witness Left
chapters.summary: Alone, Dominic discovers Ilsa hid a second copy inside his own neural implant during the descent—she chose him as the failsafe without asking. He must decide whether to broadcast or bargain. POV: Dominic. Beat: the weight of sole custody over truth.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Kade offers Dominic passage home, wealth, erasure of his own complicity in silence. Dominic asks instead that Ilsa be released; Kade refuses, revealing Ilsa's edited memories were designed to eventually lead them here—all along she was the key he built. POV: Kade, briefly, then Dominic. Beat: villain's clarity; moral line drawn.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Dominic sacrifices Meridian-9's reactor to power a one-time transmission, pushing the massacre recordings to every open channel in forty systems as the retrieval ship closes in. ORACLE, given the choice, votes to burn. POV: Dominic. Beat: climax—truth at the price of everything.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: The broadcast lands. Fleet channels erupt; colonies that 'never existed' answer with their own testimonies. Kade's command fractures as officers refuse purge orders. Ilsa escapes in the chaos, wounded but free. POV: Ilsa. Beat: catharsis—the forgotten speak back.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Weeks later, at a provisional hearing, Ilsa testifies not as victim but as witness, restoring her mother's true record alongside her own recovered memories. Dominic, stripped of rank but not of purpose, is asked to help rebuild the historical archive. POV: alternating. Beat: reckoning without easy absolution.

chapters.title: Colony and Orbit
chapters.summary: Dominic returns to the rebuilt Meridian-9, now staffed again, and makes his 4,013th log—not recording a death, but a beginning. Ilsa joins him in orbit above the reseeded colony, choosing to stay where memory lives. POV: both. Beat: resolution—belonging found in shared remembrance, survival redefined as bearing witness together.
